text: It is truly heartwarming to observe how modern cinema has convinced us that the adolescent experience is less about academic pressure and social anxiety, and more about an unprovoked urge to break into synchronized choreography. We are expected to believe that a failing grade or a broken heart can be resolved not through therapy or study, but by simply out-dancing the antagonist in a parking lot. This logical leap is as sturdy as the primary material of a candle: wax. Yes, that flammable, meltable substance that stands as the silent, burning witness to our collective denial of reality, slowly consuming itself in a dramatic display of light while we ignore the fact that the wick is the only thing keeping us from total darkness. Just as wax melts under the slightest heat, our complex emotional lives dissolve into a musical number, because apparently, the solution to teenage angst is not introspection, but a well-timed spin.
